references.text: The Lord promises that Israel will lend to many nations, but will not need to borrow themselves, as part of the blessings for obedience.
Israel shall be the head and not the tail; they shall be above and not below - parallel to the promise to rule over the nations.
In contrast to the blessing - under the curse, foreigners will lend to Israel, and they will become the tail instead of the head.
God's promise to Abraham that his offspring will take possession of their enemies' gates and that all nations will be blessed through him.
The Lord's blessing over all the work that Israel does, as the basis for the prosperity mentioned in 15:6.
The condition for the blessing: obedience to the Lord's commands will lead to there being no poor among them.
The righteous person lends and gives, as a manifestation of God's blessing upon His people.
The one who borrows is a slave under the lender - illustrating the power dynamic described in Deuteronomy 15:6.
